name: 255. Code mode replies carry what the script returns, and failed calls are values the script handles (code-mode-replies) [SERIAL]
description:
Every nested response used to be echoed into the executeToolCode reply as a `[TOOL] ... response:` line (up to 2 KB each), and every successful run ended with an environment footer, so a script returning one number still sent the model every payload it read. A call that answered with `isError` (how mcp-go and most SDK servers report a failure) reached the script as a plain string that looked like a normal result. These cases pin that the reply carries only what the script prints and returns, that a failed call reaches the script as an error value (`hasattr(r, "error")`, `r.error`) and is noted in the reply with an honest status line, that `fail()` makes the run an error, and that a script which recovers from a failed call still succeeds. The SSE fixture's `echo` returns `isError` with plain text when called without a message.

Serial, and it provisions its own client for the same reason as folder 210: a code-mode client makes the four meta-tools visible to every MCP-bearing request while it exists.
